simple.meaning: קָדֵשׁ (qâdêsh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a (quasi) sacred person , i.e. (technically) a (male) devotee (by prostitution) to licentious idolatry.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, Job, beginning at Deuteronomy 23:18. Its contexts include family, kingship, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָדֵשׁ (H6945).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

occurrences.englishText: You shall not bring the hire of a prostitute, or the wages of a male prostitute,* literally, dog into the house of Yahweh your God for any vow; for both of these are an abomination to Yahweh your God.
There were also sodomites in the land. They did according to all the abominations of the nations which Yahweh drove out before the children of Israel.
He put away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
There was no king in Edom. A deputy ruled.
He broke down the houses of the male shrine prostitutes that were in Yahweh’s house, where the women wove hangings for the Asherah.
